---
title: "16S amplicon data processing with DADA2 (one dataset)"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
params:
  dataset: ""            # name of the dataset, e.g. its BioProject (required); results go to <out_dir>/<dataset>/
  fastq_dir: ""          # folder with the paired-end reads, named <sample>_1.fastq[.gz] and <sample>_2.fastq[.gz] (required)
  trunc_len_f: -1        # truncation length of the forward reads, chosen from the quality plots (required)
  trunc_len_r: -1        # truncation length of the reverse reads (required)
  quality_only: false    # true: only draw the quality plots, to choose the truncation lengths, and stop
  out_dir: "results/amplicon"
  genus_dir: "results/amplicon/genus_tables"   # the genus table of this dataset, input of the merging document
  silva_db: "databases/silva/silva_nr99_v138.1_wSpecies_train_set.fa.gz"
  multithread: true
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
stopifnot("set the parameters 'dataset' and 'fastq_dir'" = nzchar(params$dataset) && nzchar(params$fastq_dir))
```

## To perform ASV based analysis, we directly load paired-end reads fastq files in R and perform processing through dada2

```{r load-reads}
library(dada2)
path <- params$fastq_dir #directory containing fastq files
list.files(path)
```

## Sorting of fastq files

```{r sort-files}
fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_1.fastq", full.names=TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_2.fastq", full.names=TRUE))
stopifnot("no forward/reverse read pairs found in fastq_dir" = length(fnFs) > 0 && length(fnFs) == length(fnRs))
```

## Extraction of sample names having extension ".fastq"

```{r sample-names}
sample.names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(fnFs), "_"), `[`, 1)
```

## Inspecting read quality profiles

```{r quality-profiles}
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[1:2]) #forward reads
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[1:2]) #reverse reads
```

```{r quality-only, include = FALSE}
# with quality_only the document ends here: choose trunc_len_f and trunc_len_r from the plots above
if (isTRUE(params$quality_only)) knitr::knit_exit()
```

```{r check-parameters, include = FALSE}
trunc_f <- params$trunc_len_f
trunc_r <- params$trunc_len_r
stopifnot("set trunc_len_f and trunc_len_r (use quality_only first to look at the quality plots)" = trunc_f >= 0 && trunc_r >= 0)
stopifnot("Silva training file not found: run scripts/setup_silva_database.sh" = file.exists(params$silva_db))
ds_dir <- file.path(params$out_dir, params$dataset)       # all results of this dataset
filt_dir <- file.path(ds_dir, "filtered")
dir.create(filt_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(params$genus_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Assigning the filenames for the filtered fastq.gz files

```{r filenames}
filtFs <- file.path(filt_dir, paste0(sample.names, "-F-filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path(filt_dir, paste0(sample.names, "-R-filt.fastq.gz"))
```

## For filtering of reads

```{r filter-reads}
for(i in seq_along(fnFs)) { fastqPairedFilter(c(fnFs[i], fnRs[i]), c(filtFs[i], filtRs[i]), truncLen=c(trunc_f, trunc_r), maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ=2, compress=TRUE, verbose=TRUE) }
```

## Sample inference

```{r sample-inference}
derepFs <- derepFastq(filtFs, verbose=TRUE)
derepRs <- derepFastq(filtRs, verbose=TRUE)
names(derepFs) <- sample.names
names(derepRs) <- sample.names
dadaFs <- dada(derepFs, err=inflateErr(tperr1,3), selfConsist = TRUE, MAX_CONSIST=20)
dadaRs <- dada(derepRs, err=inflateErr(tperr1,3), selfConsist = TRUE, MAX_CONSIST=20)
```

## Merging of paired reads

```{r merge-pairs}
mergers <- mergePairs(dadaFs, derepFs, dadaRs, derepRs, verbose=TRUE)
head(mergers[[1]])
```

## Constructing sequence table

```{r sequence-table}
seqtab <- makeSequenceTable(mergers)
dim(seqtab)
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab))) #Inspecting distribution of sequence lengths
```

## Removing chimeras

```{r chimeras}
seqtab.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab, method="consensus", multithread=params$multithread, verbose=TRUE)
dim(seqtab.nochim)
sum(seqtab.nochim)/sum(seqtab)
```

## Assigning taxonomy

```{r taxonomy}
taxa <- assignTaxonomy(seqtab.nochim, params$silva_db, multithread=params$multithread)
```

## Inspecting the taxonomic assignments

```{r inspect-taxonomy}
taxa.print <- taxa
rownames(taxa.print) <- NULL
head(taxa.print)
```

## Extracting the count values and the sequences from dada2 output

```{r write-dada2-output}
# giving our seq headers more manageable names (ASV_1, ASV_2...)
asv_seqs <- colnames(seqtab.nochim)
asv_headers <- vector(dim(seqtab.nochim)[2], mode="character")

for (i in 1:dim(seqtab.nochim)[2]) {
  asv_headers[i] <- paste(">ASV", i, sep="_")
}

# making and writing out a fasta of our final ASV seqs:
asv_fasta <- c(rbind(asv_headers, asv_seqs))
write(asv_fasta, file.path(ds_dir, "ASVs.fa"))

# count table:
asv_tab <- t(seqtab.nochim)
row.names(asv_tab) <- sub(">", "", asv_headers)
write.table(asv_tab, file.path(ds_dir, "ASVs_counts.tsv"), sep="\t", quote=F, col.names=NA)

# taxonomy table:
rownames(taxa.print) <- rownames(asv_tab)
head(taxa.print)
write.table(taxa.print, file.path(ds_dir, "ASVs_taxonomy.tsv"), sep="\t", quote=F, col.names=NA)
```

## Now, we load phyloseq for further analysis of the amplicon data

```{r phyloseq}
library(phyloseq)
seq <- as.matrix(seqtab.nochim)+1 # for removing zeroes from the count table
tax <- taxa
dim(seq)
colnames(seq) <- paste0("ASV_", seq_len(ncol(seq))) #for giving unique ASV Ids to each sequence
rownames(tax) <- colnames(seq)
ps <- phyloseq(otu_table(seq, taxa_are_rows=FALSE), 
               tax_table(tax))
ps1 <- ps #assigning all the information of ps to a new object ps1
rank_names(ps1) # check the taxonomy levels
#Removing sequences not aligning to the bacteria
ps1a <- subset_taxa(ps1,Order!="Chloroplast")
ps1b <- subset_taxa(ps1a,Family!="Mitochondria")
ps1 <- subset_taxa(ps1b,Kingdom!="Archaea")
ps
ps1
count <- t(ps1@otu_table)
write.table(count, file.path(ds_dir, "ps1_ASVs_counts.tsv"), sep="\t", quote=F, col.names=NA) ## writing a new count file
write.table(ps1@tax_table, file.path(ds_dir, "ps1_ASVs_taxonomy.tsv"), sep="\t", quote=F, col.names=NA) ## writing a new taxonomy file
```

## Genus table of this dataset

This step was added so that the workflow runs without manual editing. The merging document needs one table per dataset:
a `Genus` column followed by one column per sample, with the ASVs as rows. ASVs without a genus assignment are
dropped, because they cannot be merged by genus. Note that the counts of `ps1` include the `+1` added above.

```{r genus-table}
count_m <- as(count, "matrix")
genus <- as(tax_table(ps1), "matrix")[rownames(count_m), "Genus"]
genus_table <- data.frame(Genus = genus, count_m, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
genus_table <- genus_table[!is.na(genus_table$Genus), ]
write.table(genus_table, file.path(params$genus_dir, paste0(params$dataset, ".tsv")),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
dim(genus_table)
```
